title: 'Gen Z not anti-national': RSS chief backs protest, seeks facts on police action
content: Calling "protest is a way of dialogue", RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said: "I won’t say that Gen Z should not protest, but in a democracy there are ways of going about it". He said that Gen Z and Gen Alpha want "logical answers" to the questions raised by them. The RSS chief also said that the "education is not a commercial business". Earlier, Bhagwat urged parents to lead by example.

title: Meta admits to 'serious issues' in talks with govt over CSAM, deepfakes & bots
content: Meta's international team is in ongoing talks with Indian government representatives today, aiming to align with local laws and tackle content moderation challenges. Officials are requesting insights into algorithms and preventive measures against harmful content. They are also discussing WhatsApp policies and strategies to combat CSAM. A meeting between IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Meta's global team is expected later today.

title: 'Neeche baith ke rah': Jaiswal recalls Rohit Sharma's scolding in Insta post
content: Jaiswal shared a set of pictures from India's training session as preparations began for the two-Test series. However, it was his caption that caught the attention of fans.

title: Merchant charges for UPI soon? LS passes Bill allowing banks to levy fees
content: This empowers the government to allow banks and other payment service providers to impose charges on transactions conducted through the unified payments interface (UPI) and other electronic payment modes that may be notified.

title: Kentucky family rejects $26M offer for farm land over ‘poison’ data center
content: A Kentucky family has taken a stand against a tempting $26 million proposal for their farmland, which an undisclosed company intended for a grand AI data center. The family champions the importance of preserving agricultural land and food security, emphasizing that their attachment to the property goes beyond mere monetary value. In contrast, other local landowners appear to be more receptive to selling.

title: 'Auqib Nabi shouldn't have come as a replacement': Ex-cricketer on India squad
content: Auqib Nabi earned a place in India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka series. He replaces the injured fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah in the team. Nabi's selection follows his strong performances in domestic cricket competitions. He took 104 wickets across two exceptional Ranji Trophy seasons. Nabi becomes the first cricketer from Jammu and Kashmir to reach this milestone.

title: 'Save me': Eyewitness recounts Atiq Ahmed son's final moments after fatal crash
content: Abaan Ahmed, the youngest of Atiq Ahmed's children, tragically passed away in a road accident in Jhansi. His SUV hit a divider, resulting in his immediate death and that of a friend. Three other friends sustained injuries and are under medical care. Investigators are looking into differing accounts surrounding the crash. The burial of Abaan Ahmed is planned for Friday in Prayagraj.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.

title: Oregon vet left $150K job to soft-retire; relief work now pays twice as much
content: Coco Gauff’s rise to Grand Slam success is also the story of her family’s belief. Her parents changed their lives to support her dream, stayed by her side through pressure and celebrated every milestone with her. From Wimbledon at 15 to the 2023 US Open title, Gauff’s journey shows how faith, sacrifice and family can shape a champion.

title: Woman tries steak after 14 years vegan; emotional video hits 20M views
content: A TikTok video showing a woman eating steak for the first time after following a vegan diet for 14 years has gone viral, drawing around 20 million views. She became emotional after taking her first bite, while her husband comforted and encouraged her without pressure. Many social media users praised his supportive reaction as much as her heartfelt experience.

title: After 'ban' on Claude Code, Microsoft has more 'bad news' for Anthropic
content: Microsoft has told engineers that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for" in a new internal memo from EVP Jay Parikh. The memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default internal model, replacing an auto-router that had been sending GitHub Copilot workloads to Anthropic's Claude. Every Microsoft division now carries an AI token budget target, months after Claude Code licences were cancelled.

title: On the frontlines: How Indian sailors are paying the price in Middle East war
content: India's maritime workers are confronting unprecedented challenges as wartime conflicts reconfigure shipping routes into perilous zones. The recent loss of life among Indian sailors in attacks on commercial vessels has raised alarm. With many enduring extended time away from home and facing harsh conditions at sea, their families live in constant worry about their safety. The call for better protection and governmental assistance for these seafarers is intensifying.

title: Watch: Indian-origin Nasa astronaut Anil Menon embarks on historic ISS spacewalk
content: Indian-origin NASA astronaut Anil Menon just accomplished his inaugural spacewalk outside the International Space Station alongside astronaut Jessica Meir. This essential task involved enhancing the power system of the ISS, ensuring its energy supply remains sustainable for many future missions. Menon's milestone underscores India’s expanding role in global space exploration and innovation.

title: AIFF considers withdrawing from FIFA ASEAN Cup in favour of India vs Brazil game
content: AIFF is weighing the option of withdrawing from the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup or fielding a second-string side to prioritise the October 3 friendly against Brazil. While most Executive Committee members favour the marquee clash, former India captain Bhaichung Bhutia has urged the federation to back the tournament for its sporting and financial benefits.

title: How Cambridge's youngest black professor 'conned' Great Britain
content: How did Jason Arday’s extraordinary claims travel from interview to interview without serious scrutiny? His rise and fall tells a larger story about Cambridge, imperial guilt, institutional theatre and the modern Britain that wanted to believe.

title: England recall Cook, Ollie Pope for Pakistan Tests; Joe Root to lead
content: Ollie Pope, Dan Lawrence and Sam Cook have all returned to the Test squad, while Jordan Cox is also back and is expected to bat at No. 3, according to The Guardian. Cox gets the opportunity after Jacob Bethell was ruled out of the series with an injury.

title: 'Political victim like Umar Khalid': Tarun Tejpal seeks leniency in rape case conviction
content: The Bombay high court has recently convicted Tarun Tejpal in connection with a 2013 rape case, resulting in a ten-year term of rigorous imprisonment after his acquittal was set aside. Tejpal, alleging political victimization, appealed for leniency, while the court has provided him with a two-week window to surrender. This verdict is linked to a reported incident in a hotel elevator that occurred thirteen years prior.

title: 'No one was allowed': Rahane reveals MS Dhoni's one strict rule
content: Mahendra Singh Dhoni fostered a comfortable team atmosphere with his open hotel room policy.  Younger players often gathered there for relaxation and games away from cricket pressure.  Ajinkya Rahane shared insights into this inclusive team culture during a recent interview.  Rahane recently announced his retirement from all forms of cricket after a distinguished career.  Dhoni's own playing future remains uncertain following an injury and missed IPL season.

title: 'Kya Bolti Public': CJP announces nationwide 'pressure campaign' from September
content: The Cockroach Janata Party is stepping in as a public pressure group, primarily targeting pressing issues such as unemployment and education reform across the country. Set to launch their 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign in September, they aim to engage the youth in dialogue for transparency and accountability. Moreover, the CJP is determined to tackle escalating education costs and improve the reliability of media.

title: 'Soren unfit to hold office': Protesting students demand Jharkhand CM resign
content: Gearing up for assembly "gherao" on August 10 in the backdrop of the ineffective redressal, a protester said: "We remain steadfast until the government accepts our demands. We now demand the chief minister's resignation, as he is unfit for the office he holds. It has been so long since he returned from Bengaluru, yet he has taken no cognisance of the situation."

title: India gets its first woman 'Top Gun': Bhawana Kanth scripts IAF history
content: Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth achieved a historic milestone by clearing the Fighter Combat Leader course. This demanding program trains officers in advanced combat tactics and spans twenty weeks. She is the first woman pilot from the Indian Air Force to achieve this distinction. The Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment is a premier institution for operational edge. This achievement highlights continued progress for women in the Indian Air Force.

title: 'It means I've played a bit': Starc on verge of breaking Kapil Dev's Test record
content: Australian pacer Mitchell Starc is just one wicket away from equaling the legendary Kapil Dev's career tally. As he sets his sights on surpassing Dale Steyn's remarkable wicket record, Starc emphasises the importance of continuous improvement over personal achievements. This mindset has played a crucial role in his enduring success on the field.

title: Who is Lucky Rawat? India's only student selected for North Pole mission
content: Fifteen-year-old Lucky Rawat from Uttarakhand's Chakrata has been chosen as India's sole student representative for the prestigious Icebreaker of Knowledge Arctic expedition. After clearing a rigorous international selection process, he is joining students from 22 countries on a scientific voyage to the North Pole, highlighting how talent and perseverance can open extraordinary global opportunities.

title: 'Lot of workload': Ex-cricketer explains why Bhuvi, Shami's comeback is difficult
content: Aakash Chopra expresses concerns about Bhuvneshwar Kumar's chances for the 2027 World Cup, pointing to his limited workload. He highlights the importance of continuous preparation in 50-over formats beyond the IPL. Meanwhile, Mohammad Shami appears to be in a stronger position for selection.

title: Taxation bill clears Lok Sabha, allows provision for MDR on UPI transactions
content: Under the proposed changes, the Central government would be empowered to specify, through a notification, the electronic payment modes or transactions that must continue to remain free of charges.

title: Scientists reveal how green roofs cut rooftop temperatures by 40°F
content: Green roofs offer a solution to urban heat by absorbing sunlight and releasing water. Vegetation shades surfaces and evapotranspiration naturally cools surrounding areas. These living roofs also manage rainwater and provide habitats for urban wildlife. Extensive and intensive systems cater to different building needs and budgets. Cities worldwide are adopting green roofs to combat rising temperatures and improve environments.

title: Most expensive surface warship programme? US Navy's Trump-class battleship could cost $275 billion
content: A new Congressional Budget Office report details the US Navy's proposed Trump-class battleship program. This ambitious fleet of fifteen vessels is projected to cost an estimated $275 billion over nearly three decades. The program's high expense stems from the ships' unprecedented size and advanced nuclear propulsion systems. Meeting the planned schedule would require doubling large surface combatant production by 2035.

title: 'Convey sentiments to Amit Shah': RS Chair to Rijiju after oppn seeks his presence
content: Parliament proceedings faced disruptions as opposition parties demanded Union home minister Amit Shah's statement. Rajya Sabha Chairman asked Kiren Rijiju to convey the opposition's sentiments to the home minister. Mallikarjun Kharge reiterated the demand for a statement and discussion on the police action. Rijiju said Kharge had not cited any rule while making the request.

title: Why analogue paneer is booming in India — and why states are cracking down
content: Analogue paneer, a cheaper substitute, is now facing strict government action.  Gujarat and Maharashtra have banned its sale due to adulteration concerns.  These states are prioritizing consumer protection over mere labelling violations.  The crackdown highlights the growing problem of food adulteration across India.  This move signals a significant shift in regulatory enforcement for dairy products.

title: From Bhargavastra to Indrajaal: How India's drone killers take on hostile UAVs, swarms
content: India is rapidly developing advanced counter-drone systems to counter aerial threats.  Indigenous systems like Bhargavastra and Indrajaal offer diverse engagement capabilities.  BEL's D4 system integrates multiple neutralization methods onto a single platform.  The DRDO's precision-guided munitions extend aerial threat engagement options.  These developments position India to effectively manage evolving drone warfare challenges.

title: 100% tariffs: Why India may ignore Trump threat and continue buying Russian oil
content: A year since the whole penal tariff cycle began - India now faces uncertainty related to its Russian crude purchases. A new Russia related sanctions bill in the US may see the light of the day if passed this year implying that Trump would have the power to impose tariffs on India again.

title: 81 years after Hiroshima, Indian subcontinent most at risk of nuclear flashpoint
content: The article details the historical introduction of nuclear weapons and their proliferation. India and Pakistan possess comparable nuclear arsenals, with differing strategic doctrines. India maintains a No First Use policy and a credible minimum deterrent. Pakistan employs full-spectrum deterrence, offsetting conventional military inferiority. These divergent approaches shape the strategic balance and potential for conflict in South Asia.

title: Tarun Tejpal to move SC after Bombay HC conviction in rape case
content: The Bombay high court convicted Tarun Tejpal of rape and outraging modesty. This verdict overturned his previous acquittal by a Goa sessions court. Tejpal stated he is a political victim and will appeal the high court's decision. Former investigating officer and Advocate General welcomed the judgment for justice. The case involved allegations from a junior colleague in 2013.

title: BAI promises best-ever BWF World Championships after India Open controversy
content: The upcoming World Championships will showcase the newly revamped venue promised by the Badminton Association of India. With all prior issues from the India Open being resolved, the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium has received comprehensive upgrades. Malaysian lighting specialists have been engaged to ensure stellar conditions. Anticipation builds for what is expected to be the most remarkable BWF World Championships India has ever hosted.

title: Trump administration refunds $100 billion in tariffs struck down by US Supreme Court
content: In a significant move, the Trump administration has reimbursed nearly one hundred billion dollars in tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled against wide-ranging duties. By July, around sixty percent of these tariffs were refunded to importers. The court's decision emphasized that the existing law did not provide blanket authority for imposing tariffs. Moving forward, Trump is leveraging alternative legal channels to impose new tariffs.

title: Neil Armstrong's boyhood home built in 1908 hits market for $430,000
content: For sale is the childhood home of Neil Armstrong in Wapakoneta, Ohio, a historic two-storey residence that has been lovingly preserved for nearly forty years. This house boasts many original features that tie it to the first man on the Moon, making it a site of interest for history buffs and space enthusiasts alike. The current owner hopes the new buyer will continue to honor its significant legacy.
